questions.q: What problem does compliance as code solve that a quarterly manual audit does not?
options: It eliminates the need for any human review ever
It closes the gap between audits by running checks continuously, so drift is caught quickly
It makes compliance optional for regulated data
It replaces the need for a qualified PCI-DSS assessor entirely
questions.explain: A system can drift out of compliance the day after a manual audit passes. Compliance as code runs the same check continuously, so drift is caught between audit cycles instead of at the next one.

questions.q: In the Chef InSpec control shown in this lesson, what does the 'impact' field represent?
options: How long the check takes to run
The severity or criticality rating of the control
The number of resources it checks
The name of the person who wrote it
questions.explain: Impact is a weighted value (0 to 1) describing how critical a control is, with values closer to 1.0 indicating higher severity findings.

questions.q: Why is Northbridge Retail in scope for PCI-DSS?
options: Because it uses Azure for its infrastructure
Because it is an e-commerce retailer that processes customer payment data
Because it has more than 100 employees
Because it runs containers in production
questions.explain: PCI-DSS applies to any organization that stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data. Northbridge Retail handles customer payments, which puts it in scope.

questions.q: A compliance control runs daily and logs a timestamped pass or fail result. What is this record an example of?
options: A vulnerability report
Continuous evidence that can support a compliance assessment
A threat model
A secrets detection finding
questions.explain: Timestamped, repeated control results form continuous evidence — exactly the kind of record an auditor can use to confirm controls were working between formal assessments.

questions.q: Does passing automated compliance-as-code checks replace a formal PCI-DSS assessment?
options: Yes, automated checks are legally equivalent to a formal assessment
No — it produces continuous evidence that supports and speeds up a formal assessment, but does not replace it
Yes, but only for Requirement 10
No, automated checks have no value to an assessor
questions.explain: Compliance as code produces ongoing evidence that controls are working, which makes a real assessment by a qualified assessor faster and more thorough — it does not substitute for that formal review.
